Into thy hou{{ls}}e.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Exteriour {{ls}}ignes of more then common deuotion.}}An exceding approbation of the extraordinary workes and {{ls}}ignes of external deuotion, vvhich {{ls}}eeme to carnal men (though othervvi{{ls}}e faithful) to be often {{ls}}uperfluous or not acceptable. This Simon vvas perhaps of a good vvil, and therfore (as diuers others did els where) inuited Chri{{ls}}t to his hou{{ls}}e, not of curio{{ls}}itie or captiou{{ls}}nes, as {{ls}}ome other did: but of affection, as it may {{ls}}eeme by Chri{{ls}}ts familiar talke with him. Notwith{{ls}}tanding his duties towardes him were but ordinary. but the anointing, wa{{ls}}hing, ki{{ls}}{{ls}}ing, wiping of his feete in {{ls}}uch {{ls}}ort as the woman did, were further {{ls}}ignes of more then vulgar loue: {{ls}}uch as is in deuout men or women that goe on pilgrimage and ki{{ls}}{{ls}}e deuoutly the holy memories of Chri{{ls}}t and his Saincts. Which is no more but an exteriour expre{{ls}}{{ls}}ing of their affection, and that they loue much, as euery vulgar chri{{ls}}tian man doth not.

Thy faith.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Iu{{ls}}tification attributed not to faith onely.}}The remi{{ls}}{{ls}}ion of her {{ls}}innes being attributed before to charitie, is novv al{{ls}}o {{ls}}aid to come of her faith. Whereby you may know that it commonly procedeth of both, and of hope al{{ls}}o, though but one named. Becau{{ls}}e vvhen there be diuers cau{{ls}}es concurring to one effect, the {{ls}}criptures commonly name but one, and that e{{ls}}pecially vvhich is mo{{ls}}t proper to the purpo{{ls}}e and time, not excluding the other. And therfore his working miracles vpon any per{{ls}}on, is attributed to the faith of them on whom or at who{{ls}}e de{{ls}}ire they be done. Becau{{ls}}e he vvrought his miracles to induce al men to beleeue in him, and therfore {{ls}}pecially required faith at their hands, and namely before other things, vvhether they did beleeue that he vvas able to doe that which they a{{ls}}ked at his hands: without vvhich it had ben rather a mockrie and tentation of him, then a true de{{ls}}ire of benefite at his hands.
